drug_class: Selective norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor (SNRI) — non-stimulant ADHD medication
purpose: Viloxazine is used to treat Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) in children, teenagers, and adults. It helps improve focus, reduce impulsivity, and manage hyperactivity. It is a non-stimulant option, which means it works differently from medications like Adderall or Ritalin.
how_it_works: Your brain uses a chemical messenger called norepinephrine to help with attention and self-control. Viloxazine works by blocking the recycling of norepinephrine back into brain cells, so more of it stays available where it is needed. This helps the parts of your brain that manage focus and behavior work more effectively.
common_side_effects: Sleepiness or fatigue, decreased appetite, nausea or upset stomach, headache, irritability, and trouble sleeping. Some people may also notice a slightly increased heart rate or blood pressure. Most side effects are mild and often improve after the first few weeks.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you have a history of heart problems, high blood pressure, or seizures, as viloxazine may affect these conditions. It can increase thoughts of suicide or self-harm, especially in children and teenagers — contact your doctor right away if you notice any mood changes or unusual thoughts. Do not take it with MAO inhibitors (a type of antidepressant), as this combination can be very dangerous. Avoid alcohol while taking this medication.
typical_dosing: For children ages 6 to 11, the usual starting dose is 100 mg once daily in the morning, which may be increased up to 400 mg per day. For teens and adults, dosing typically starts at 200 mg once daily and can go up to 400–600 mg per day. Capsules can be swallowed whole or opened and sprinkled on soft food like applesauce. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions.
